explanation: A diffraction grating with N lines per millimeter has slit spacing d = 1/N, so its principal maxima obey d sinθ = mλ — the same condition as two slits, but the many slits make each order sharp and bright. More lines/mm means a smaller d, which throws each order to a larger angle and spreads the spectrum; eventually high orders disappear once mλ/d exceeds 1 (sinθ can't exceed 1). The animation fans out the visible orders for 550 nm light and labels each angle. On the AP exam this is used to find wavelength from a measured angle, or to count how many orders a grating can produce.
bullets: Each diffracted ray is an order m where d sinθ = mλ; m=0 is the straight-through beam.
More lines/mm shrinks d, so the same order m appears at a larger angle θ.
Orders exist only while mλ/d ≤ 1 — the readout shows the highest visible order.
Spacing d (nm) and first-order angle θ(m=1) update live as you change lines/mm.
